[{"id":"f-lol-cap-bf0febde","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ VI SERVICER AND MARKETING AGENT","rationale":"The liability architecture sits at or above the fallback on its material terms and is not adverse to us. (1) Mutuality: Section 6.2(a) (p0283) limits Cellco as Servicer/Marketing Agent to its specific obligations and to its own willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, and Section 5.2(a) (p0243) applies word-for-word the same limitation to the Depositor — the exculpation is symmetric in structure. (2) No monetary cap: there is no aggregate liability cap, no fee-based ceiling and no \"shall not exceed\" formula anywhere in the document (Section 9.7 is only a trustee capacity carve-out; Section 9.6 is limited recourse). The absence of a cap means the counterparty's exposure — including its Section 6.3 indemnities (p0291–p0292) for willful misconduct, bad faith and gross negligence in favour of the Issuer and the trustees — is uncapped, so the fallback carve-outs for indemnification, gross negligence and wilful misconduct are satisfied a fortiori. Inserting a mutual 12-months-of-fees cap would newly cap Cellco's uncapped indemnity and exculpate it above a Servicing Fee-based ceiling; that would weaken our position, so we do not redline it. (3) Our own exposure is additionally protected, not exposed: Section 9.6 (p0378) confines any claim against the Depositor or the Issuer to the Depositor Transferred Property only — a one-sided de facto limit in our favour, with no equivalent limit for Cellco. Walk-away triggers are absent: our liability is not uncapped while Cellco's is capped, there is no sub-6-month cap, and indemnities are not inside any cap. Noted short of preferred, but not flagged: there is no free-standing mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages (the bar on punitive and consequential damages at p0469 binds only the arbitral panel in dispute resolution proceedings), no USD 1,000,000 floor, no express confidentiality/data-protection or IP-infringement super-carve-outs, and no statement that payment obligations are outside the cap. Each of these is a preferred-only refinement that has no adverse effect while no cap exists.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-f2b1dab4","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ X MISCELLANEOUS","rationale":"Section 10.2(a) is the operative assignment clause. Our side is protected on the outbound leg: Section 5.3 (p0249) lets the Depositor pass this Agreement to a merger/consolidation successor, a person succeeding to its business, or an Affiliate, and Section 10.2(a) expressly excepts Section 5.3 from the consent requirement. Section 7.1 (p0314) also bars the Servicer from resigning except on legal inability, so a change of control on our side gives Cellco no exit. The clause fails on the inbound leg. Section 10.2(a) requires consents from the Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee, Certificateholders and Noteholders, but not from the Issuer or the Depositor, so we hold no consent right over a Servicer assignment; the consent standard is unqualified rather than \"not unreasonably withheld\"; there is no bar on assignment to a competitor; and the Section 7.6 carve-out (p0348) lets Cellco assign to any Cellco Affiliate with no consent or notice at all, which also defeats the fallback requirement that every non-successor assignment need consent. The redline removes the Section 7.6 exception for the Servicer only, adds the Issuer's reasonable consent, and adds a competitor bar, leaving Section 5.3 and the Section 7.4 successor-servicer mechanics intact. Ancillary point noted but not flagged: Section 6.4 (p0300) allows consent-free delegation while Cellco remains Servicer, but delegation does not relieve Cellco of responsibility.","proposal":"Require the Issuer's reasonable consent to any Servicer assignment (including to a Cellco Affiliate) and bar assignment to a competitor, leaving the Depositor's Section 5.3 affiliate/successor rights untouched.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-b2aa43a0","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on our side, so it meets the preferred position and needs no redline. The operative engagement provisions are bare appointments of Cellco as Servicer (p0080), Custodian (p0137) and Marketing Agent (p0150) with no \"sole and exclusive\" designation, no requirements commitment, and no covenant barring the Issuer or Depositor from procuring comparable services from third parties; Article VII expressly permits terminating the Servicer and installing a Successor Servicer. The only instances of \"exclusive\" are unrelated: \"exclusive control\" over the Cap Collateral Account (p0387-p0388) is a securities-account control mechanic held by the Issuer, and p0388 in fact constrains the Issuer's own exercise of it, so it runs in our favour rather than against us; and p0427 refers to \"nonexclusive jurisdiction,\" a forum term outside this rule. Because no exclusivity binds us, the fallback's category, 12-month, and performance-exit limits are not engaged.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-b5ee025a","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ VIII TERMINATION","rationale":"The agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum/early-termination fee on the Issuer or Depositor in favour of Cellco, so the preferred position is met. The only premium-style amount is the Make-Whole Payment (Sections 8.1-8.2; definition at Appendix A), which is a yield-maintenance amount payable to Noteholders on a voluntary Optional Redemption elected by the Class A Certificateholder and funded through the agreed waterfall — it is investor economics, not a breach-triggered liquidated sum payable to the counterparty, and the Clean-Up Redemption is expressly available without any Make-Whole Payment. The other amounts we reviewed run the right way or are ordinary compensation: late fees, prepayment charges and other Supplemental Servicing Fees are collected from Obligors rather than paid by us; servicing-transition expenses are \"paid by the resigning or terminated Servicer\"; the Successor Servicer's $150,000 appointment fee is third-party compensation paid from the waterfall, not a penalty; and the indemnities in Section 6.3 run from the Servicer and Marketing Agent to us. No redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-2438dd24","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ VII SERVICER RESIGNATION AND TERMINATION; SUCCESSOR SERVICER","rationale":"The only licence-responsive provision is p0346, and it is an express refusal to license: the Servicer \"will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party.\" Searches for \"license\", \"grant\", \"right to use\", \"software\" and \"irrevocable\" surface nothing else in our favour: the other hits are regulatory qualification licences and security-interest \"Grants\" (defined at p0763 as a pledge, not an IP licence). The power of attorney at p0105 runs from the Issuer to the Servicer and is revocable by us, so it benefits our side and is not flagged. With no grant at all, our Affiliates are excluded with no path to add them and nothing is transferable to a successor, so the clause fails both fallback elements and sits in walk-away territory. We convert the disclaimer sentence into a licence to the Issuer at the fallback level (Affiliates on written notice; transferable to an M&A successor) and keep the retained carve-out for confidentiality- and law-restricted materials verbatim so no contradictory mechanic survives. The preferred perpetual/irrevocable, subscription-termination and contractor elements are not pursued, as this servicing structure has no paid-up or subscription licence construct.","proposal":"Convert the Servicer's express refusal to license servicing software into a licence to the Issuer, extended to Issuer Affiliates on written notice and transferable to an M&A successor.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-c53470a2","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","rationale":"The agreement contains no non-compete, field-of-use, territory or exclusivity covenant binding the Issuer or the Depositor, so the preferred position is met. Searches for \"compete\", \"competing\", \"exclusive\", \"field of use\", \"engage\", \"solicit\", \"restriction\" and \"prohibited\" across Articles I–XI and the schedules return only (i) \"court of competent jurisdiction\" references (p0335, p0469), (ii) generic no-conflict representations that performance will not contravene \"any contractual restriction binding on or affecting it or its property\" (p0240, p0266, p0279), and (iii) the Cap Collateral Account \"exclusive control\" account-control mechanic (p0387–p0388), none of which limit the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build. The Servicer engagement in Section 3.1 is not stated to be exclusive, and the successor-servicer provisions expressly contemplate our engaging another institution to service the Receivables (p0334, p0346). The restrictions we do carry — Section 9.2 (no transfer or Lien on Depositor Transferred Property), Section 9.5 (no petition) and Section 9.6 (limited recourse) — are structural securitization covenants protecting the transaction's bankruptcy-remote status, not restrictive covenants against competing activity, and Section 7.3's limit on the Servicer's obligation to license its own software is a restriction on Cellco's obligations rather than on our business. No redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-5fc74b00","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"needs_review","sectionRef":"§ VII SERVICER RESIGNATION AND TERMINATION; SUCCESSOR SERVICER","rationale":"The Agreement runs until the last Receivable is paid in full or the Issuer is terminated (Section 8.3), a multi-year term. Our only exit is cause-based: under Section 7.2(c) the Servicer may be removed solely if a Servicer Termination Event occurs and is continuing, and no at-will or convenience right exists anywhere for the Issuer or Depositor, who are the customer side here. The Optional Acquisition and Optional Redemption in Sections 8.1 and 8.2 are conditional Class A Certificateholder options (10% pool threshold; February 2021 date plus Make-Whole Payment; Administrator consent), not a customer convenience right. That is the walk-away case of no customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months, so the fallback is not met on its material terms. The Vendor side already exceeds both levels: Section 7.1 bars the Servicer from resigning except on legal inability, so that preferred element is already met and is left untouched (moving to the fallback would hand the Servicer an end-of-term convenience right it does not have). I therefore target preferred and insert only the missing customer convenience right, drafted as a new Section 7.2(e) removal reaching the Servicer's rights and obligations under this Agreement. Placing it inside Section 7.2 makes it a removal pursuant to that Section, so the Cellco reassumption in Section 7.2(c) engages, and Section 7.4(a)(i) is triggered whenever the Servicer \"resigns or is terminated under this Agreement\", which is party-agnostic and needs no conforming language for an Issuer-initiated removal. Section 8.3's Agreement-level triggers are untouched, and Section 7.3 fixes effectiveness at the date stated in the notice of termination. Servicing Fees are payable in arrears on each Payment Date, so the refund limb is protective only.","proposal":"Add Section 7.2(e) letting the Issuer, as customer, remove the Servicer for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro rata refund of prepaid Servicing Fees","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-audit-11082b8c","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","rationale":"The AUDIT rule constrains audit/inspection rights that bind us. Searching the full document for audit, inspection, examination, verification, records and access surfaced only two review clauses, and both run in our favour rather than against us. Section 3.6 (p0131) obliges the Servicer (Cellco, the counterparty) to give the Issuer, Depositor, Administrator, Owner Trustee and Indenture Trustee access to its records to review the Servicer's performance, and Section 3.9(e) (p0146) obliges the Custodian (also Cellco) to give the Depositor, Issuer and Indenture Trustee access to the Receivable Files and receivables systems. The remaining hits are the same direction: p0437 requires the Servicer to deliver records to the Administrator and Issuer for Regulation AB compliance, and p0446-p0447 require the Servicer to grant the Asset Representations Reviewer access. Cellco has no reciprocal right to audit, inspect or access the Issuer's or Depositor's records or systems, so none of the walk-away triggers (unlimited or unannounced audits, remote access to our systems) is present and there is no counterparty audit right to which the frequency, notice and cost parameters could attach. Nothing here is adverse to us and no redline is warranted. Two observations noted but not flagged: the planner's question whether the policy qualifiers gut our access, i.e. that our review rights under Sections 3.6 and 3.9(e) are \"subject to the Servicer's security, confidentiality and privacy policies and any regulatory, legal and data protection policies\", concerns the strength of our own inspection rights and is outside this rule's checklist, which only limits audits against us; expanding our access would fall under a separate audit-rights-in-our-favour position. Likewise the requirement that access be exercised \"by all parties at the same time\" at the Servicer's offices is a constraint on our own right, not an obligation imposed on us.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-79330f7a","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ X MISCELLANEOUS","rationale":"Section 10.5 (p0426) makes the internal laws of the State of New York the governing law (expressly invoking N.Y. Gen. Oblig. Law §§ 5-1401/5-1402) and even bars amendment to any other governing law, so the preferred law element is satisfied outright. Section 10.6 (p0427) submits both parties to the SDNY and New York State courts sitting in New York, New York, with waiver of venue and forum non conveniens objections; that submission is non-exclusive rather than exclusive, which is a minor shortfall from the preferred wording only and is noted rather than redlined — the forum sits well above the fallback (Delaware/California/London) and nowhere near walk-away territory. The Section 11.2 dispute resolution mechanic (p0450) is elective, available only to a Requesting Party for unresolved reacquisition/acquisition requests after 180 days, and any mediation or arbitration is seated in New York, New York (p0473) under JAMS/AAA rules, so there is no mandatory or foreign-seated arbitration. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-indemn-cf3eceff","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ VI SERVICER AND MARKETING AGENT","rationale":"Section 6.3 runs in our favour but is textually short of the preferred position on five counts: the indemnity is not an express duty to defend (Section 6.3(b) is permissive - the Servicer \"may participate in and assume the defense\"), the Indemnified Person definition reaches the Issuer, Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee and their officers, directors, employees and agents but not the Issuer's Affiliates, and the triggers are exhaustively \"willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence\", with no violation-of-Law, data-breach or intellectual-property-infringement limb, and no cooperation covenant. We have repaired each in the shortest operative form: \"will defend and indemnify\" plus \"and its Affiliates\" in Section 6.3(a)(i) and \"will defend and indemnify\" in (a)(ii); a new (a)(iii) adding violation of Law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Obligor data or Receivable Files (Cellco acts as Custodian of the Receivable Files), and third-party IP infringement or misappropriation claims for services or deliverables provided under the Transaction Documents; and a reasonable-cooperation sentence after the defence-assumption mechanics. We deliberately did not touch the permissive assumption of defence in Section 6.3(b), because it allocates control of the defence and the conditional mechanics in the following paragraph (\"If the Servicer ... notifies the Indemnified Person of its intention to assume the defense\") depend on it. We also did not import the fallback's 3x annual fees super-cap - Section 6.3 is presently uncapped, which is better for us - and we added no Issuer or Depositor indemnity, since none exists today (Section 9.2 is a narrow defence-of-title covenant). If the business confirms the transaction has no services, deliverables, software or IP-licence subject matter, limb (C) can be dropped as scoped out.","proposal":"Make Cellco's Section 6.3 indemnity a defence obligation running to the Issuer's Affiliates and add limbs for violation of Law, data breach and IP infringement, plus a cooperation sentence.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-mfn-a2344fe4","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ IX OTHER AGREEMENTS","rationale":"We ran independent searches for each MFN trigger (\"most favored nation\", \"no less favorable\", \"favorable\", \"terms offered to any other\", \"right to match\", \"best price/discount\", \"comparable/other transactions\"). The only near-hit is p0692, which uses \"pricing new issues of corporate debt securities of comparable maturity\" as a discount-rate convention for a note payment calculation, not a terms-comparison mechanic. The covenant articles (Article IX Other Agreements, Article VI Servicer and Marketing Agent) impose transfer, lien, expense and servicing covenants but no obligation on the Issuer or Depositor to extend Cellco terms no less favourable than those given to third parties, and no right-to-match or best-terms disclosure mechanic. There is therefore no MFN obligation burdening our side (and none granted in our favour), which satisfies the preferred position that Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor. No redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-8a1b2105","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","rationale":"The agreement imposes no minimum purchase or volume commitment on us. Our only compensation obligation to Cellco is the Servicing Fee, payable solely \"As compensation for performing its obligations under this Agreement\" and calculated as \"one-twelfth of the Servicing Fee Rate\" (0.75%) times \"the Adjusted Pool Balance\" — i.e., a purely usage/asset-based fee for services actually rendered, with no floor, minimum, take-or-pay, or shortfall penalty. Likewise the Supplemental Servicing Fee and Temporarily Excluded Receivables Servicing Fee are computed on actual Recoveries and actual Principal Balances. Acquisitions of Additional Receivables (Sections 2.1(b) and 2.1(d)) are conditional transfers with no committed minimum volume or frequency, and no volume cap restricts us. Searches for \"minimum\", \"commit\", \"volume\", \"take or pay\" and \"obligated to purchase\" returned no obligation running against us. The two \"shortfall\" hits confirm the planner's read and run in our favour or against third parties: the Marketing Agent's Credit Payment deposit obligation on a \"shortfall in Collections\" (p0211) is a payment to us, and the requirement that \"The customer is required to purchase a new qualifying device\" (p0595) is an upgrade-offer condition on Obligors, not on the Issuer or Depositor. This sits at the preferred position (no minimum commitment; fees for services actually performed), so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-f71df7ff","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ VI SERVICER AND MARKETING AGENT","rationale":"The Agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binding the Issuer or Depositor (our parties), and none binding Cellco either. Targeted searches for \"solicit\", \"no-hire\", \"induce\", \"hire\", \"personnel/recruit/staff\" and \"non-compete/restrictive covenant\" returned no hits anywhere in the document. Every occurrence of \"employee\"/\"employ\" is unrelated to restrictive covenants: the no-recourse-against-individuals clauses (p0244, p0284, quoted above), the \"Indemnified Person\" definition in the Servicer indemnity (p0291), the ERISA/Benefit Plan definitions (p0649, p0651, p0740), and the Independent Manager eligibility definition (p0770). Article VII (Servicer Resignation and Termination; Successor Servicer) — the provision where a servicing-transfer employee restriction would typically sit — likewise contains no such language.\n\nThis meets the preferred position (\"No non-solicit on Customer\") in full, so the fallback's narrowing elements (mutuality, personnel directly involved, 12-month tail, general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, no no-hire) are not reached. The absence of any restriction operates entirely in our favour and is not redlined; no elementCoverage is mapped because a compliant finding proposes no operation and the preferred element is satisfied by the absence of clause text rather than by any quotable provision. No action required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-57c46a06","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ VIII TERMINATION","rationale":"This is a securitization transfer and servicing agreement with no term-and-renewal structure. Searches for \"renew\", \"automatically renew\", \"extension/expiration/successive/anniversary\" and any fee-uplift mechanic returned no renewal provision anywhere: Article VIII (Sections 8.1-8.3) provides only optional acquisition/redemption and a single termination trigger, and Section 8.3 runs the Agreement until the last Receivable is paid in full, settled, sold or written off or the Issuer is terminated under the Trust Agreement. Because there is no automatic renewal, every conditional element of the preferred position (12-month renewal terms, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder, CPI/3% uplift cap) is satisfied vacuously, and there is no non-renewal notice window or price-escalation mechanic that could fall into fallback or walk-away territory (no multi-year auto-renewal, no >90-day notice window). Any extension of the deal would have to be effected by amendment, which Section 10.1(a) frames as an act of \"the parties\", i.e., by mutual written agreement, consistent with the preferred position. Nothing here is adverse to us, so no redline is warranted; we record RENEWAL as not applicable to this term structure.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-d8bab96d","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ VII SERVICER RESIGNATION AND TERMINATION; SUCCESSOR SERVICER","rationale":"Section 7.5 does contain a transition regime: the Servicer must cooperate in an orderly transition on resignation or termination (p0343) and must transfer funds and deliver the Receivable Files and records to the Successor Servicer (p0344/p0346), with the custodian delivering Receivable Files on termination of that appointment (p0147). It fails the fallback on two material terms: there is no minimum transition assistance period, and delivery of files and records is only \"as soon as practicable\", with no 30-day outside date. We therefore target the fallback with the two shortest conforming edits: a 90-day assistance floor in 7.5(a) and a 30-day delivery deadline in 7.5(b). We have not pursued the preferred position (six months, machine-readable format, certified deletion), which is not required where the fallback is met. We note but do not redline the 7.5(b) carve-out (p0346) refusing to license servicing software or provide items restricted by confidentiality or data protection policies; it is directed at Servicer processes and third-party-restricted materials rather than the express Receivable Files and records delivery obligation, and 7.5(c) already places transition expenses on the terminated Servicer.","proposal":"Add a 90-day transition assistance period and a 30-day outside date for delivery of funds, Receivable Files and records on Servicer resignation or termination.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-warranty-4f4d7ed3","ruleId":"WARRANTY","ruleTitle":"Performance warranty and duration","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ III SERVICING OF RECEIVABLES","rationale":"This is a transfer and servicing agreement with no software, deliverables or licensed technology, so the software-conformance element has no subject matter here; the performance bargain sits at the fallback and we would not redline it. (1) Services standard: Section 3.2(a) requires Cellco to \"manage, service, administer and collect on the Receivables with reasonable care using that degree of skill and attention that the Servicer exercises for all comparable device payment plan agreement receivables that it services for itself or others according to the Servicing Procedures\", and Section 6.1(a) repeats the Servicer's representations and warranties, including compliance with Law applicable to the servicing and that \"It has complied in all material respects with the Servicing Procedures with respect to the Receivables\", as of the Closing Date and as of each Acquisition Date, expressly surviving transfer — coverage for the life of the deal, well beyond the 30-day fallback floor. (2) Repair/replacement: Section 3.3(b) gives us a notice-and-correct mechanic (quoted), and Section 7.2(a)(ii) allows removal and replacement of the Servicer for any unperformed obligation having a material adverse effect that is uncured after ninety (90) days. (3) Refund: Sections 2.5 and 3.3(d) require the Originator or Servicer to reacquire/acquire the affected Receivables by remitting the Acquisition Amount — the economic equivalent of a refund for non-conforming assets. Notably, there is no \"AS IS\" or blanket warranty disclaimer anywhere, so the walk-away position is not in play; the only no-warranty language (Section 3.3(e)) runs in our favour, being a transfer by the Issuer without recourse or warranty. Short of preferred, and noted rather than flagged: there is no express \"professional and workmanlike\" or no-malicious-code warranty, and the reacquisition/acquisition remedies are expressed as sole remedies (Sections 2.5(c), 3.3(g)). The separate liability floor of willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in Section 6.2(a) is a limitation-of-liability point and is left to that rule rather than flagged twice here.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-insurance-75a8cf0d","ruleId":"INSURANCE","ruleTitle":"Vendor insurance","severity":"low","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ X MISCELLANEOUS","rationale":"The Agreement contains no insurance covenant of any kind for the Servicer/Marketing Agent/Custodian. The only occurrences of \\\"insurance\\\" are Obligor premium charges billed to wireless accounts (p0095) and FDIC deposit insurance in the account-eligibility definition (p0903); neither imposes any coverage obligation on Cellco. Cellco services the Receivables and holds Obligor account, payment and Receivable File data, so the absence of any E&O or cyber cover falls in walk-away territory under this rule. We therefore insert a short covenant at the end of Article X (Miscellaneous) at the fallback level only — errors and omissions of $1,000,000 and cyber/privacy of $2,000,000 — rather than the preferred CGL/E&O/cyber/workers' compensation programme, which is the smallest complete change.","proposal":"Insert Section 10.14 requiring Servicer E&O insurance of $1,000,000 and cyber/privacy insurance of $2,000,000.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-811e3e75","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"low","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ VII SERVICER RESIGNATION AND TERMINATION; SUCCESSOR SERVICER","rationale":"There is no walk-away problem: nothing assigns our IP or the Receivables data to Cellco, the Receivables are expressly marked as \"owned by the Issuer\" (p0375), the Receivable Files are held for the benefit of the Issuer and Indenture Trustee, and no joint ownership is created. However, the Agreement fails the fallback: the Servicer prepares and delivers Monthly Investor Reports, Receivable Files, accounts and records for us, yet we receive no licence at all in them, while Section 7.5(b) expressly preserves the Servicer's processes, models and servicing software (which satisfies the fallback element allowing Vendor to keep its generic tools and know-how). The Servicer's access to our data is already confined to servicing purposes (p0146), so the only gap is the deliverables licence. We therefore add one short subsection to Section 9.4 granting the Issuer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense those deliverables for its business, without disturbing the Servicer's retained tools.","proposal":"Add a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence for the Issuer to use, modify and sublicense the Servicer's reports, files and records.","verification":"pass"}]

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Form of Transfer and Servicing Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Issuer / Depositor)  
**Re:** Playbook review findings, redline priorities and walk-away exposure

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed the playbook review of the Form of Transfer and Servicing Agreement. The document is structurally favourable to us on most commercial-protection rules: there is no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN, minimum-commitment or liquidated-damages obligation binding our side; governing law and venue are New York; audit and inspection rights run in our favour only; and the liability architecture is symmetric and uncapped, with Cellco's Section 6.3 indemnities sitting outside any ceiling.
